sets.title: Family puzzle
sets.stimulus:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below.

There are 6 members — P, Q, R, S, T, U — in a family of three generations. There are two married couples in the family.
Q is the wife of P.
R is the only daughter of P.
S is the brother of R.
T is the daughter-in-law of Q.
U is the son of T.
There is no single parent in the family.

questions.prompt: How is U related to R?

steps: Tree: P (male) = Q (female) → children R (female) and S (male); S = T (female) → son U (male).
R is the daughter of P and Q; S, her brother, is their son.
T is Q's daughter-in-law, so T is the wife of Q's son S; U is the son of T (and S).
U is the son of R's brother → U is R's **nephew**.
solution.trap: Son would need R to be U's parent; U's parents are S and T.

questions.prompt: Who is the grandmother of U?

steps: Tree: P (male) = Q (female) → children R (female) and S (male); S = T (female) → son U (male).
U's father is S, and S's mother is Q (the wife of P).
So **Q** is U's grandmother.
solution.trap: T is U's mother, not grandmother; P is the grandfather.

questions.prompt: How many female members are there in the family?

steps: Tree: P (male) = Q (female) → children R (female) and S (male); S = T (female) → son U (male).
"Wife" fixes Q, "only daughter" fixes R, "daughter-in-law" fixes T as female.
P (husband of Q), S (brother) and U (son) are male → female members = **3**.
solution.trap: Do not miss T: "daughter-in-law" is a female relation.

questions.prompt: If W is the husband of R, how is W related to S?

steps: Tree: P (male) = Q (female) → children R (female) and S (male); S = T (female) → son U (male).
W would be the husband of S's sister R.
The husband of one's sister is one's **brother-in-law**.
solution.trap: Son-in-law is W's relation to P and Q, not to S.

sets.title: Family puzzle
sets.stimulus:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below.

There are 7 members — A, B, C, D, E, F, G — in a family of three generations. There are two married couples in the family.
B is the husband of E.
F is the only daughter of E.
A is the sister-in-law of F.
F is not married.
C is the granddaughter of B.
G is the brother of C.
D is the father of G.
There is no single parent in the family.

questions.prompt: How is A related to E?

steps: Tree: B (male) = E (female) → children D (male) and F (female, unmarried); D = A (female) → children C (female) and G (male).
F is unmarried, so A can be F's sister-in-law only as the wife of F's brother.

C, a granddaughter of B, needs a parent among B's children. F has no children (unmarried, no single parent) and A cannot be B's daughter (F is E's only daughter), so that parent is D (father of G and C), a son of B and E.
Only two couples exist (B–E and one more), so D's wife is A. A is the wife of E's son → **daughter-in-law**.
solution.trap: Sister-in-law is A's relation to F, not to E.

questions.prompt: Who is the daughter of A?

steps: Tree: B (male) = E (female) → children D (male) and F (female, unmarried); D = A (female) → children C (female) and G (male).
A is D's wife, and D is the father of G and C.
C is a granddaughter (female) and G is a brother (male) → **C** is A's daughter.
solution.trap: F is E's daughter (A's sister-in-law), not A's.

questions.prompt: How many grandsons does B have?

steps: Tree: B (male) = E (female) → children D (male) and F (female, unmarried); D = A (female) → children C (female) and G (male).
B's grandchildren are C and G, the children of his son D (F is unmarried and has no children).
C is a granddaughter and G a grandson → B has **1** grandson.
solution.trap: F is B's daughter, not a grandchild, and C is female.

questions.prompt: If H is the husband of F, how is H related to D?

steps: Tree: B (male) = E (female) → children D (male) and F (female, unmarried); D = A (female) → children C (female) and G (male).
F is D's sister, so her husband H would be D's **brother-in-law**.
solution.trap: H would be the son-in-law of B and E, not of D.

sets.title: Family puzzle
sets.stimulus:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below.

There are 7 members — J, K, L, M, N, O, S — in a family of three generations. There are two married couples in the family.
L is the wife of K.
M has no siblings.
N is the daughter of O.
K is the father of M.
O is the son-in-law of K.
J is the sister of N.
S is the grandson of L.

questions.prompt: How is M related to K?

steps: Tree: K (male) = L (female) → only child M (female); M = O (male) → children N (female), J (female) and S (male).
M is the only child of K (M has no siblings).
O is K's son-in-law, i.e. the husband of K's daughter; K has no child other than M, so M is that daughter.
M is the **daughter** of K.
solution.trap: No clue calls M a "daughter" directly — the gender comes from "son-in-law of K"; Son ignores it.

questions.prompt: Who is the son of M?

steps: Tree: K (male) = L (female) → only child M (female); M = O (male) → children N (female), J (female) and S (male).
S is a grandson of L; L's only child is M, so S is a child of M (and O).
S is male → **S** is the son of M. N and J are daughters.
solution.trap: O is M's husband, not her son.

questions.prompt: How is K related to J?

steps: Tree: K (male) = L (female) → only child M (female); M = O (male) → children N (female), J (female) and S (male).
J is the sister of N, and N is the daughter of O; O's wife is M, so J is a child of M.
M is K's daughter → K is the **grandfather** of J.
solution.trap: Father-in-law is K's relation to O, not to J.

questions.prompt: If T is the wife of S, how is T related to O?

steps: Tree: K (male) = L (female) → only child M (female); M = O (male) → children N (female), J (female) and S (male).
S is the son of O and M.
The wife of one's son is one's **daughter-in-law**.
solution.trap: Sister-in-law would need S to be O's brother; S is O's son.

sets.title: Family puzzle
sets.stimulus:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below.

There are 7 members — P, Q, R, T, V, W, Y — in a family of three generations. There are two married couples in the family.
T is the only son of W.
V is the sister-in-law of R.
Q is the father-in-law of R.
P and Y are the children of T.
Y is the nephew of V.
W is the wife of Q.
P is not the brother of Y.

questions.prompt: How is P related to W?

steps: Tree: Q (male) = W (female) → children T (male) and V (female); T = R (female) → children P (female) and Y (male).
R is married to a son of Q; Q's only son is T (the only son of his wife W), so T = R.
P is a child of T, i.e. a grandchild of W. P is Y's sibling but not his brother → P is a sister (female).
P is the **granddaughter** of W.
solution.trap: "P is not the brother of Y" does not make P unrelated — P is still Y's sibling, so P must be his sister.

questions.prompt: How is V related to P?

steps: Tree: Q (male) = W (female) → children T (male) and V (female); T = R (female) → children P (female) and Y (male).
Only two couples exist (Q–W and T–R), so V is not the wife of R's brother; V must be the sister of R's husband T.
V is the sister of P's father T → V is P's **aunt**.
solution.trap: Mother is R, the wife of T; V is T's sister.

questions.prompt: Who is the daughter of Q?

steps: Tree: Q (male) = W (female) → children T (male) and V (female); T = R (female) → children P (female) and Y (male).
Q's children are T (son) and V, T's sister.
**V** is Q's daughter; R is his daughter-in-law and P his granddaughter.
solution.trap: R is the daughter-in-law of Q — "in-law" is not a daughter.

questions.prompt: What is the number of male members in the family?

steps: Tree: Q (male) = W (female) → children T (male) and V (female); T = R (female) → children P (female) and Y (male).
Male: Q (wife W), T (son), Y (nephew).
Female: W, V, R (daughter-in-law, as T's wife), P (not the brother) → male members = **3**.
solution.trap: P is female: a sibling who is "not the brother" is a sister.

sets.title: Family puzzle
sets.stimulus:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below.

There are 7 members — D, E, F, G, H, J, K — in a family of three generations. There are two married couples in the family.
D is the daughter-in-law of H.
K is the sister of G.
F is the granddaughter of E.
J is the brother of F.
H is the husband of E.
K is not married.
There is no single parent in the family.

questions.prompt: How is E related to D?

steps: Tree: H (male) = E (female) → children G (male) and K (female, unmarried); G = D (female) → children F (female) and J (male).
D is married to a son of H. J is a grandchild and K is a sister, so the only possible son is G; D is G's wife.
E is the mother of G (wife of H) → E is D's **mother-in-law**.
solution.trap: Mother would need D to be E's own child; D only married into the family.

questions.prompt: Who is the father of F?

steps: Tree: H (male) = E (female) → children G (male) and K (female, unmarried); G = D (female) → children F (female) and J (male).
F is a granddaughter of E, so F's parent is a child of E. K is unmarried and there is no single parent, so K has no children.
So F is the child of G (and D) → **G** is F's father.
solution.trap: H is F's grandfather.

questions.prompt: How many grandchildren does H have?

steps: Tree: H (male) = E (female) → children G (male) and K (female, unmarried); G = D (female) → children F (female) and J (male).
H's children are G and K; K is unmarried with no children.
G's children are F and J → H has **2** grandchildren.
solution.trap: D is a daughter-in-law, not a grandchild.

questions.prompt: If L is the husband of K, how is L related to F?

steps: Tree: H (male) = E (female) → children G (male) and K (female, unmarried); G = D (female) → children F (female) and J (male).
K is the sister of F's father G, i.e. F's aunt.
The husband of one's aunt is one's **uncle**.
solution.trap: Brother-in-law is L's relation to G and D, not to F.

sets.title: Family puzzle
sets.stimulus:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below.

There are 7 members — L, M, N, P, Q, R, S — in a family of three generations. There are two married couples in the family.
N has no siblings.
Q is the mother of N.
M is the husband of Q.
R is the daughter-in-law of M.
S is the mother of R.
L is the daughter of R.
P is the grandson of S.

questions.prompt: How is S related to N?

steps: Tree: M (male) = Q (female) → only child N (male); S (female) → daughter R (female); N = R → children L (female) and P (male).
R is married to a son of M. M's only child is N (N has no siblings), so N is male and R's husband.
S is the mother of R, N's wife → S is N's **mother-in-law**.
solution.trap: Mother is Q, the wife of M.

questions.prompt: How is L related to M?

steps: Tree: M (male) = Q (female) → only child N (male); S (female) → daughter R (female); N = R → children L (female) and P (male).
L is the daughter of R, and R's husband is N, M's son.
So L is the **granddaughter** of M.
solution.trap: Daughter would be L's relation to N and R.

questions.prompt: Who is the husband of R?

steps: Tree: M (male) = Q (female) → only child N (male); S (female) → daughter R (female); N = R → children L (female) and P (male).
R is the daughter-in-law of M, so she is married to M's son.
M's only child is N → **N** is R's husband.
solution.trap: P is R's son (grandson of S).

questions.prompt: How many female members belong to the youngest generation?

steps: Tree: M (male) = Q (female) → only child N (male); S (female) → daughter R (female); N = R → children L (female) and P (male).
The youngest generation is N and R's children, L and P.
L is a daughter and P a grandson → **1** female member.
solution.trap: R is a daughter-in-law in the middle generation — do not count her with the youngest.

sets.title: Family puzzle
sets.stimulus:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below.

There are 8 members — S, T, U, V, W, X, Y, Z — in a family of three generations. There are three married couples in the family.
W is the son-in-law of Y.
U is the son of T.
X is the brother-in-law of W.
S is the cousin of U.
Y is the wife of V.
Z is the mother of S.
T is the only daughter of V.
S is a grandchild of V.
There is no single parent in the family.

questions.prompt: How is S related to T?

steps: Tree: V (male) = Y (female) → children T (female) and X (male); T = W (male) → son U (male); X = Z (female) → child S (gender not given).
W is married to T (Y's daughter is V's only daughter T). S, a grandchild of V, is not T's child (S is U's cousin), so S is the child of X and Z, with X the brother of T.
S is the child of T's brother → nephew or niece. No clue gives S's gender → **Cannot be determined**.
solution.trap: "Cousin of U" and "grandchild of V" are gender-neutral; picking Nephew or Niece guesses the gender.

questions.prompt: How is Z related to Y?

steps: Tree: V (male) = Y (female) → children T (female) and X (male); T = W (male) → son U (male); X = Z (female) → child S (gender not given).
S is a grandchild of V but not through T (S is only U's cousin), so S's parent X is V's son and Z, S's mother, is X's wife.
Z is the wife of Y's son → **daughter-in-law**.
solution.trap: Daughter is ruled out: T is V's only daughter.

questions.prompt: Who is the son-in-law of V?

steps: Tree: V (male) = Y (female) → children T (female) and X (male); T = W (male) → son U (male); X = Z (female) → child S (gender not given).
W is the husband of T, V's daughter → **W** is V's son-in-law.
solution.trap: X is V's own son and W's brother-in-law — not a son-in-law.

questions.prompt: If S is female, how is S related to W?

steps: Tree: V (male) = Y (female) → children T (female) and X (male); T = W (male) → son U (male); X = Z (female) → child S (gender not given).
S is the child of X, the brother of W's wife T, so W is S's uncle (by marriage).
A female S is W's **niece**.
solution.trap: Cousin is S's relation to U, W's son.

sets.title: Family puzzle
sets.stimulus:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below.

There are 8 members — A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H — in a family of three generations. There are three married couples in the family.
D is the grandson of F.
H is the only sister of D.
A is the brother-in-law of E.
G is the daughter of C.
E is the father of H.
B is the sister-in-law of G.
C is the husband of F.
G has no children.
There is no single parent in the family.

questions.prompt: How is A related to F?

steps: Tree: C (male) = F (female) → children E (male) and G (female); E = B (female) → children D (male) and H (female); G = A (male), no children.

D and H are children of E. D is F's grandson, so E or E's wife is F's child. If E's wife were F's daughter G, G would have children — but G has none. So E is the son of C and F, and E's wife is B (B is the wife of G's brother).
The third couple must be G and A: D and H are E's children, and G and A are the only two members left who can marry each other (A is male, being a brother-in-law). A is the husband of E's sister G.
A is the husband of F's daughter → **son-in-law**.
solution.trap: Son fits only the rejected case where A is G's brother; "G has no children" removes that case.

questions.prompt: Who is the daughter-in-law of C?

steps: Tree: C (male) = F (female) → children E (male) and G (female); E = B (female) → children D (male) and H (female); G = A (male), no children.
C's son E is married to B → **B** is C's daughter-in-law.
solution.trap: G is C's daughter and H his granddaughter.

questions.prompt: How many of the female members are married?

steps: Tree: C (male) = F (female) → children E (male) and G (female); E = B (female) → children D (male) and H (female); G = A (male), no children.
Married women: F (wife of C), B (wife of E) and G (wife of A, the third couple).
H is a child and unmarried → **3**.
solution.trap: No clue says "G is the wife of A" — it follows from the three couples, so do not leave G out.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true?
options: G is the aunt of D.
H is the granddaughter of A.
D is the cousin of H.
B is the daughter of F.
E is the son-in-law of C.

steps: Tree: C (male) = F (female) → children E (male) and G (female); E = B (female) → children D (male) and H (female); G = A (male), no children.
G is the sister of D's father E → G is D's aunt (true).
B is F's daughter-in-law, H is A's niece, E is C's son and D is H's brother — the other four are false.
solution.trap: E is C's son; the son-in-law of C is A.

sets.title: Family puzzle
sets.stimulus:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below.

There are 8 members — K, L, M, N, O, P, Q, R — in a family of three generations. There are three married couples in the family.
Q is the only child of M.
L is the son-in-law of R.
O is the brother-in-law of L.
K is the father-in-law of M.
N is the grandmother of Q.
P is the husband of R.
O is not married.
There is no single parent in the family.

questions.prompt: How is R related to L?

steps: Tree: K (male) = N (female) → son L (male); P (male) = R (female) → children M (female) and O (male, unmarried); L = M → only child Q (gender not given).
M's husband is K's son. The only men who can be married in the middle generation are L and O, and O is unmarried, so M is L's wife.
L is R's son-in-law, so M is R's daughter → R is L's **mother-in-law**.
solution.trap: Mother is N: N is Q's other grandmother, so she must be L's mother (M's parents are P and R).

questions.prompt: Who is the mother-in-law of M?

steps: Tree: K (male) = N (female) → son L (male); P (male) = R (female) → children M (female) and O (male, unmarried); L = M → only child Q (gender not given).
M's husband L is the son of K; N, a grandmother of Q who is not M's mother, is K's wife and L's mother.
**N** is M's mother-in-law.
solution.trap: R is M's own mother.

questions.prompt: If S is the wife of O, how is S related to M?

steps: Tree: K (male) = N (female) → son L (male); P (male) = R (female) → children M (female) and O (male, unmarried); L = M → only child Q (gender not given).
O is the brother of M (O is L's brother-in-law and unmarried, so he is the brother of L's wife M).
The wife of one's brother is one's **sister-in-law**.
solution.trap: Daughter-in-law is S's relation to P and R.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is NOT true?
options: N is the mother-in-law of M.
K is the grandfather of Q.
P is the father-in-law of L.
O is the uncle of Q.
R is the grandmother of O.

steps: Tree: K (male) = N (female) → son L (male); P (male) = R (female) → children M (female) and O (male, unmarried); L = M → only child Q (gender not given).
R is O's mother, not grandmother → this statement is false.
O is the brother of Q's mother (uncle, whatever Q's gender); K and N are L's parents; P is M's father → the other four are true.
solution.trap: "O is the uncle of Q" is true even though Q's gender is unknown — uncle describes O, not Q.

sets.title: Family puzzle
sets.stimulus:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below.

There are 8 members — S, T, U, V, W, X, Y, Z — in a family of three generations. There are three married couples in the family.
Y has only one son.
S is the sister-in-law of Z.
X is the son-in-law of W.
T is the granddaughter of Y.
V is the brother of T.
Z is the mother of V.
Y is the wife of W.
Z has no siblings.
There is no single parent in the family.

questions.prompt: How is X related to V?

steps: Tree: W (male) = Y (female) → children U (male) and S (female); U = Z (female) → children T (female) and V (male); S = X (male), no children.
T and V are Z's children and grandchildren of Y, so Z or Z's husband is Y's child. Z has no siblings, so Z is not Y's child; Z's husband is Y's only son — call him U.
S, sister-in-law of Z, is then U's sister (the third couple is not available for "wife of Z's brother" since Z has no brother). X, son-in-law of W, is the husband of W's daughter S.
X is the husband of V's father's sister → **uncle**.
solution.trap: Father is U; X married into the family through S.

questions.prompt: Who is the brother-in-law of U?

steps: Tree: W (male) = Y (female) → children U (male) and S (female); U = Z (female) → children T (female) and V (male); S = X (male), no children.
U's sister S is married to X, and U's wife Z has no siblings.
So **X** is the only brother-in-law of U.
solution.trap: V is U's son; W is U's father.

questions.prompt: How many members of the family have no siblings?

steps: Tree: W (male) = Y (female) → children U (male) and S (female); U = Z (female) → children T (female) and V (male); S = X (male), no children.
Sibling pairs: U and S (children of W and Y), T and V (children of U and Z).
W, Y, Z (stated) and X have no sibling in the family → **4**.
solution.trap: U's sibling S is easy to miss: she is the sister-in-law of Z and the wife of X.

questions.prompt: If R is the son of X, how is R related to V?

steps: Tree: W (male) = Y (female) → children U (male) and S (female); U = Z (female) → children T (female) and V (male); S = X (male), no children.
R would be the child of X and his wife S, and S is the sister of V's father U.
Children of a brother and a sister are **cousins**.
solution.trap: Nephew would be R's relation to U and Z, not to V.

sets.title: Family puzzle
sets.stimulus:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below.

There are 8 members — B, C, D, F, G, H, J, K — in a family of three generations. There are three married couples in the family.
G is the wife of the only son of H.
J is the granddaughter of D.
F is the son-in-law of D.
C is the brother of J.
K is the sister-in-law of G.
H is the mother-in-law of F.
C is the nephew of F.
There is no single parent in the family.

questions.prompt: How is K related to J?

steps: Tree: D (male) = H (female) → children B (male) and K (female); B = G (female) → children C (male) and J (female); K = F (male), no children.
H is F's mother-in-law, so H is female and F is the husband of H's daughter; with no single parent, H's husband D is the other parent. G is married to H's only son, B.
J (with her brother C) is D's grandchild. C is F's nephew, so C and J are not F's own children — they are the children of B and G. F's wife, D's daughter, is K (the sister of B).
K is the sister of J's father B → **aunt**.
solution.trap: Mother fits only if J were the child of F and K — "C is the nephew of F" rules that out.

questions.prompt: Who is the daughter of D?

steps: Tree: D (male) = H (female) → children B (male) and K (female); B = G (female) → children C (male) and J (female); K = F (male), no children.
D's children are B (the only son) and K, the wife of D's son-in-law F.
**K** is D's daughter.
solution.trap: G is the daughter-in-law and J the granddaughter.

questions.prompt: How many members belong to the second generation?

steps: Tree: D (male) = H (female) → children B (male) and K (female); B = G (female) → children C (male) and J (female); K = F (male), no children.
Second generation: B and K (children of D and H) and their spouses G and F.
C and J are the third generation → **4**.
solution.trap: Spouses who marry into the family belong to their partner's generation — count G and F.

questions.prompt: If M is the daughter of F, how is M related to B?

steps: Tree: D (male) = H (female) → children B (male) and K (female); B = G (female) → children C (male) and J (female); K = F (male), no children.
M would be the daughter of F and his wife K, and K is B's sister.
The daughter of one's sister is one's **niece**.
solution.trap: Cousin is M's relation to B's children C and J.

sets.title: Family puzzle
sets.stimulus:
Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below.

There are 8 members — L, M, N, P, R, S, T, V — in a family of three generations. There are two married couples in the family.
T has two daughters.
N is the only son of P.
S is the daughter-in-law of T.
L is the sister of R.
V is a grandchild of P.
M is a sibling of V.
R is the aunt of M.
There are five female members in the family.
P is the husband of T.
There is no single parent in the family.

questions.prompt: Who is the granddaughter of P?

steps: Tree: P (male) = T (female) → children N (male), L (female) and R (female); N = S (female) → two children M and V, one a boy and one a girl (which is which is not fixed).
S, T's daughter-in-law, is the wife of T's only son N. With just two couples (P–T and N–S) and no single parent, L and R have no children, so V and M are the children of N and S.
Fixed females: T, S, L, R (sisters/aunt) = 4. Five females in all means exactly one of M and V is female, but no clue says which.
The granddaughter is **either M or V**.
solution.trap: Choosing M or V alone assumes a gender that no clue fixes; "sibling" and "grandchild" are gender-neutral.

questions.prompt: How is S related to L?

steps: Tree: P (male) = T (female) → children N (male), L (female) and R (female); N = S (female) → two children M and V, one a boy and one a girl (which is which is not fixed).
T's two daughters must be L and R (R is an aunt, L her sister; S is only a daughter-in-law).
S is the wife of N, the brother of L → **sister-in-law**.
solution.trap: Daughter-in-law is S's relation to P and T.

questions.prompt: How many of the eight members are male?

steps: Tree: P (male) = T (female) → children N (male), L (female) and R (female); N = S (female) → two children M and V, one a boy and one a girl (which is which is not fixed).
Females: T, S, L, R and exactly one of M/V = 5.
Males: P, N and the other of M/V → **3**.
solution.trap: The count is fixed even though M's and V's individual genders are not.

questions.prompt: If V is the brother of M, how is M related to R?

steps: Tree: P (male) = T (female) → children N (male), L (female) and R (female); N = S (female) → two children M and V, one a boy and one a girl (which is which is not fixed).
If V is a brother, he is the male child, so M is the female child (one of the two is female).
M is the daughter of R's brother N → M is R's **niece**.
solution.trap: "V is the brother of M" fixes V as male; M's gender follows from the count of five females, so Nephew is wrong.

questions.prompt: How is C related to G?

steps: Tree: A (male) = E (female) → children G (male) and L (female); C (female) → children J (male) and N (female); G = N → son Q (male); J = L, no children.
Q, E's only grandchild, is L's nephew, so Q is the child of a son of E and A. N's husband is a son of A; of the possible men, J has no children, so N's husband is G and Q is the son of G and N.
Q is also C's grandchild; Q's father G is A's son, so C is N's mother. N is the daughter of L's mother-in-law, so C is L's mother-in-law: L (E's daughter) is married to C's son J, N's brother.
C is the mother of G's wife → **mother-in-law**.
solution.trap: Mother is E, the wife of A.

questions.prompt: How is L related to Q?

Q is the son of G and N. L is G's sister (and also the wife of N's brother J).
Either way L is Q's **aunt**.
solution.trap: Sister-in-law is L's relation to N, not to Q.

questions.prompt: Who is the son-in-law of E?

steps: Tree: A (male) = E (female) → children G (male) and L (female); C (female) → children J (male) and N (female); G = N → son Q (male); J = L, no children.
E's daughter L is married to J (L's mother-in-law is C, the mother of J and N).
**J** is E's son-in-law.

The three couples are A–E, G–N and J–L.
**J and L** is the only pair listed that is married.
solution.trap: J and N are siblings (both C's children); G and L are siblings (both E's children).

sets.title: Family puzzle

questions.prompt: How is R related to T?

steps: Tree: B (male) = K (female) → children H (male) and D (female, unmarried); F (female) → children M (female) and R (male, unmarried); H = M → children P (male) and T (female).
P and T are M's children. T is B's granddaughter, so M or her husband is a child of B (and of B's wife K). M cannot be K's daughter — D is K's only daughter — so M is married to a son of B.

H is married (F is his mother-in-law) and only two couples exist (B–K and M's), so H is that son and M's husband, and M is F's daughter. R, unmarried, can be H's brother-in-law only as the brother of H's wife M.
R is the brother of T's mother → **uncle**.
solution.trap: Brother-in-law is R's relation to H, not to T.

questions.prompt: How is F related to P?

steps: Tree: B (male) = K (female) → children H (male) and D (female, unmarried); F (female) → children M (female) and R (male, unmarried); H = M → children P (male) and T (female).
F is the mother of M, and M is the mother of P.
F is P's **grandmother** (maternal).
solution.trap: Mother-in-law is F's relation to H.

questions.prompt: If R is married to D, how is R related to H?

steps: Tree: B (male) = K (female) → children H (male) and D (female, unmarried); F (female) → children M (female) and R (male, unmarried); H = M → children P (male) and T (female).
R is already the brother of H's wife M; after the marriage he is also the husband of H's sister D.
Both links make R H's **brother-in-law**.
solution.trap: Son-in-law would be R's relation to B and K.

questions.prompt: How many female members are there in the second generation?

steps: Tree: B (male) = K (female) → children H (male) and D (female, unmarried); F (female) → children M (female) and R (male, unmarried); H = M → children P (male) and T (female).
Second generation: H and D (children of B and K), M and R (children of F).
Females: D (daughter) and M (mother) → **2**.
solution.trap: R is male (he is a brother-in-law), and F belongs to the first generation.

Married: J, S, E, N, W and W's wife (C or K).
Unmarried: the other of C and K, and G → **2**, whichever daughter W married.

J's father is a brother of B, E's father has the sister F, and D has exactly three children — so they are B, F and H (J's father), with B = C → E and H = G → J (G is A's daughter-in-law).

C is the wife of B, and B is the brother of H.

D's sons are B and H; their wives C and G are D's daughters-in-law.

C is the wife of J's father's brother B, so C is J's aunt and J is C's nephew → true.
E is A's granddaughter, B is E's father, F is J's aunt and H is D's son — the other four are false.

sets.title: Family puzzle

questions.prompt: How is K related to P?

M's wife must be N: K is L's mother and L has no siblings, so K is not P's mother, and R and S are grandchildren. So P and Q are both children of M and N.
L has no siblings, so Q can be L's brother-in-law only as the brother of L's spouse — P. K, R's grandmother, has only one child, L, so R and S are children of L and P; P is female, so L is male.

Q is the brother of R's mother → **uncle**.

Females fixed by the clues: K (mother), N (wife of M), P (daughter), R (sister) — already four.

questions.prompt: If T is the wife of Q, how is T related to S?

The wife of one's uncle is one's **aunt**.

questions.prompt: How is Q related to X?

P, the mother of S, is V's only daughter (S is the son of that daughter). Q, R's son-in-law, must be married to a daughter of R — that is P.
X is V's child, so X is P's brother. Q is the husband of X's sister → **brother-in-law**.
solution.trap: Son-in-law is Q's relation to R and V, not to X.

questions.prompt: How is S related to W?

steps: Tree: R (male) = V (female) → children P (female), T (male) and X (male, unmarried); T = U (female) → daughter W (female); P = Q (male) → son S (male).
W's father T is the brother of X, and R is W's grandfather, so T is a son of R and V; T is married to U (X is unmarried, so U is the wife of X's brother).
S is the son of P and W the daughter of T; P and T are siblings → S and W are **cousins**.
solution.trap: Brother would need S and W to share parents; S's parents are P and Q.

questions.prompt: How many sons does R have?

steps: Tree: R (male) = V (female) → children P (female), T (male) and X (male, unmarried); T = U (female) → daughter W (female); P = Q (male) → son S (male).
R's children are P, T and X (X is a child of V, R's wife; T is W's father and X's brother).
P is a daughter → R has **2** sons, T and X.
solution.trap: Q is R's son-in-law, not a son.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is NOT true?

U is the daughter-in-law of V.

T and P are both children of R and V, so T is P's brother, not her brother-in-law → this statement is false.
U is the wife of V's son T; X is the brother of S's mother; Q is married to R's daughter; P is the sister of W's father — the other four are true.
solution.trap: T is the brother-in-law of Q, not of P.

sets.title: Family puzzle
sets.stimulus:

questions.prompt: How is H related to C?

steps: Tree: A (male) = B (female) → sons C (male) and D (male); C = E (female) → only child G (male); D = F (female) → children H (female) and K (male).
E, A's daughter-in-law, is married to a son of A; G is E's only child, so H and K (G's cousin and his sister) are not E's children.

If E's husband were D, the third couple would be C and F with children H and K — but then F would be C's wife, not her sister-in-law. So E is married to C (A's son), and the third couple is D and F, the parents of H and K.
H is the daughter of C's brother D → **niece**.
solution.trap: Daughter would make H the child of C and E, but G is E's only child.

questions.prompt: Who are the grandsons of B?

steps: Tree: A (male) = B (female) → sons C (male) and D (male); C = E (female) → only child G (male); D = F (female) → children H (female) and K (male).
B's grandchildren are G (son of C and E), and H and K (children of D and F).
H is female (sister, niece). "A has two grandsons", so the other two, G and K, are both male → **G and K**.
solution.trap: G's gender is not given by any relation word ("only child", "cousin"); it comes from "A has two grandsons", so picking K alone is wrong.

questions.prompt: How many cousins does G have?

steps: Tree: A (male) = B (female) → sons C (male) and D (male); C = E (female) → only child G (male); D = F (female) → children H (female) and K (male).
G is the only child of C and E; C's brother D has two children, H and K.
G has **2** cousins.
solution.trap: G is an only child, so H and K are not his siblings — both are his cousins.

questions.prompt: How is E related to K?

steps: Tree: A (male) = B (female) → sons C (male) and D (male); C = E (female) → only child G (male); D = F (female) → children H (female) and K (male).
K is the son of D and F; E is the wife of D's brother C.
The wife of one's father's brother is one's **aunt**.
solution.trap: Sister-in-law is E's relation to D, not to K.

sets.title: Family puzzle
sets.stimulus:

questions.prompt: Who is the daughter of T?

steps: Two trees fit: N (male) = T (female) → son J (male) and a daughter, who is either X or L; J is married to the other of X and L, and V (male) is married to N's daughter. R (female) is J's daughter and P (male) is V's son.
J (father of R) and V's wife are T's children: R and P are cousins and both are T's grandchildren, so J is T's son and V (son-in-law of N) is married to T's daughter.
L and X are sisters-in-law: one is J's wife and the other T's daughter (V's wife). Either arrangement satisfies every clue.
T's daughter is **either L or X**.

questions.prompt: How is V related to J?

steps: Two trees fit: N (male) = T (female) → son J (male) and a daughter, who is either X or L; J is married to the other of X and L, and V (male) is married to N's daughter. R (female) is J's daughter and P (male) is V's son.
In both trees V is the husband of T's daughter, and J is T's son.
V is the husband of J's sister → **brother-in-law**.
solution.trap: Son-in-law is V's relation to N and T.

questions.prompt: How is T related to V?

steps: Two trees fit: N (male) = T (female) → son J (male) and a daughter, who is either X or L; J is married to the other of X and L, and V (male) is married to N's daughter. R (female) is J's daughter and P (male) is V's son.
V is N's son-in-law, i.e. the husband of a daughter of N and T.
T is the mother of V's wife → **mother-in-law**, whichever of L and X that wife is.

questions.prompt: How many married men are there in the family?

steps: Two trees fit: N (male) = T (female) → son J (male) and a daughter, who is either X or L; J is married to the other of X and L, and V (male) is married to N's daughter. R (female) is J's daughter and P (male) is V's son.
Married men: N (husband of T), J (married to X or L) and V (son-in-law of N).
P is a child → **3** in both trees.
solution.trap: Which woman J married is not fixed, but that he is married is.

items.prompt: Pointing to a boy in a photograph, Nikhil said, 'He is the only son of my father's sister.' How is the boy in the photograph related to Nikhil?

steps: "My father's sister" = Nikhil's aunt (bua).
Her son is the child of Nikhil's parent's sibling → **cousin**.
solution.shortcut: Decode the sentence from the end ("my …") backwards, one relation at a time; check whether an "only son/daughter" is the speaker.
solution.trap: Nephew would be the son of Nikhil's own sister, not of his father's sister.

items.prompt: Pointing to a woman in a photograph, Arvind told his friend, 'Her mother is the wife of my father's only son.' How is the woman in the photograph related to Arvind?

steps: Arvind is male ("his friend"), so his father's only son is Arvind himself.
Her mother is Arvind's wife, so the woman is Arvind's **daughter**.
solution.shortcut: Decode the sentence from the end ("my …") backwards, one relation at a time; check whether an "only son/daughter" is the speaker.
solution.trap: Niece assumes "my father's only son" is a brother of Arvind; a man with no brother is his father's only son himself.

items.prompt: Pointing to a girl in a photograph, Rohit told his friend, 'Her father is the son-in-law of my mother.' How is the girl in the photograph related to Rohit?

steps: Rohit is male, so his mother's son-in-law is the husband of Rohit's sister.
The girl is the daughter of Rohit's sister → **niece**.
solution.shortcut: Decode the sentence from the end ("my …") backwards, one relation at a time; check whether an "only son/daughter" is the speaker.
solution.trap: Daughter would need Rohit to be the son-in-law himself; a son-in-law of Rohit's mother cannot be her own son.

items.prompt: Pointing to a man in a photograph, Anita said, 'His wife is the only daughter of my husband.' How is the man in the photograph related to Anita?

steps: Anita's husband's only daughter is Anita's daughter too (a child of a married man is the child of his wife).
The man is the husband of Anita's daughter → **son-in-law**.
solution.shortcut: Decode the sentence from the end ("my …") backwards, one relation at a time; check whether an "only son/daughter" is the speaker.
solution.trap: Brother-in-law would be the husband of Anita's sister, not of her daughter.

items.prompt: Pointing to a man in a photograph, Tenzing said, 'The wife of his only son is the mother of my brother.' How is the man in the photograph related to Tenzing?

steps: The mother of Tenzing's brother is Tenzing's mother; her husband is Tenzing's father.
So the man's only son is Tenzing's father → the man is Tenzing's (paternal) **grandfather**.
